componentMapping: chemistry > periodic-table > Metal/Nonmetal/Metalloid/Noble-gas specimen set (metalloid/semiconductor-family candidate) -- fills part of Gap B from docs/assets/chemistry-structure.md. NOTE: this is silicon carbide (SiC), a semiconductor compound crystal, not elemental silicon -- the wave-1 brief asked for a "silicon wafer/ingot" specimen; no CC0/CC-BY-no-auth elemental-silicon crystal was found this wave either (see gaps doc), so this is documented as the closest genuinely-licensed substitute, not a literal match.
underlyingStructureData: Unit cell of silicon carbide, alpha polytype (2H-SiC), per-entry description: "Unit cell of silicon carbide Alpha (2H-SiC) - STL file"
molecularFormula: SiC (2H polytype, hexagonal wurtzite-type unit cell)
creator: feriousfabrious (farzin.jahangiri@gmail.com)
attributionText: Not legally required. Recommended credit: "Silicon Carbide 2H", NIH 3D (3d.nih.gov, entry 3DPX-008102), by feriousfabrious. CC0 1.0.
redistributionStatus: Unrestricted (CC0 public domain dedication). Confirmed via NIH 3D entry page license badge linking to the CC0 1.0 deed.
downloadedVariant: Silicone Carbide Crystal_0_NIH3D.glb (source filename has a typo, "Silicone" for "Silicon"; kept as downloaded, our file is correctly named crystal-silicon-carbide-2h-nih.glb). .stl/.wrl/.x3d variants also exist on the entry and were not downloaded.

validation.generator: https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh (STL-to-GLB conversion of a 3D-printable unit-cell model, not an authored-for-web asset)

reviewNote: Structural GLB validation and license verification only. Single untextured mesh, no material assigned by source (converted from a 3D-print STL). Content note (SiC vs elemental Si) must be preserved if this is wired in a future wave, so the component label stays scientifically accurate.
